name: tensortransit
status: 0.2.1 -- the 0.2 core is now in the MEASURED path. The SparkInfer adapter and the synthetic benchmark drove the 0.1 CudaLocalityController directly through 0.2.0, so a contributor who wrote a planner changed nothing about the measured end-to-end number; both now route through TensorRegistry -> TransitGraph -> ITransitPlanner -> CudaTransitExecutor, with the 0.1 controller kept as TENSORTRANSIT_ENGINE=v0 so the migration is an A/B in one binary rather than an assertion. MEASURED, one box, one model load, the only variable being the engine: v0 +0.115% at a 0.075% floor, transit +0.145% at a 0.109% floor, both token-exact, both 96 windows attached to captured graph nodes, both 0 capture invalidations (results/rtx5090-0.2.1-rewiring-check.json). The adapter registers KV, so the second proof track can be measured at all. The linear cost model -- under which greedy-on-density was provably optimal and the whole admission axis measured nothing -- is replaced by a residency model fitted to the paired hardware arms in results/ (rms 0.271 against the linear model's 0.485 points; 8 of 8 arms inside their own noise floor against 6 of 8), superlinear in residency, so concentrating beats spreading. And the XS/S/M/L/XL impact bands are gone: their lowest paying step was 2% weighted throughput gain and the physical ceiling for the whole shipped policy family is 0.52% on the scored model, so a submission could remove every recoverable byte and score `none`. What replaces them is the Transit Frontier Ledger -- continuous Frontier Gain over a Pareto hypervolume of goodput against p99 inter-token latency, frozen TTF generations, a paired bootstrap as a qualification gate, a protected-workload guard, and permanent append-only Frontier Receipts.
core: software-directed CUDA locality for mutable recurrent LLM state, embeddable in an inference runtime, with enumerated optimization surfaces measured against a real model rather than a microbenchmark
validated: Zero-warning CUDA build on sm_120; compute-sanitizer (memcheck, initcheck, synccheck, racecheck) clean over BOTH engines; install + find_package; a documented API/ABI stability contract with static_asserts a consumer's own build runs; a standalone probe that reads an access-policy window back off a graph captured with the attribute set mid-capture, at 1 to 128 nodes; and a fabricated device-capability matrix that needs no GPU (A100-like, H100-like, a part whose persisting L2 is smaller than one layer's state, one with more persisting L2 than the whole footprint, one reporting zero, and one whose two capacity numbers contradict). The check COUNTS are in `checks` below and are regenerated by scripts/manifest.py --with-checks <build> from the suites' own output; they used to be typed here, and they drifted.
regenerate: scripts/manifest.py  (--check is what CI runs; --with-checks <build> re-runs the suites)
